display: Daniel Koh, scout for an Asia-focused indie game publishing fund in Singapore. Ex-producer with four shipped titles, I play about 300 demos a year and attend festivals in Tokyo, Seoul, Jakarta, Shanghai and elsewhere.

signals.text: I'm in the middle of the autumn scouting cycle: 160+ demos played, and the submission window closes on 2 November.
I'm flying to Shanghai on 16 October for an indie festival and would like to meet teams and people there.
I keep meeting promising place-specific games that have no original audio yet, and I wish I knew more composers and sound designers who want to work on games.
I keep meeting gifted solo developers, artists and musicians who can't pass our first filter alone, and I'd like to point them toward collaborators.
I've seen a lot of competent but forgettable pixel-art roguelikes this cycle. I'd much rather see something unexpected.
I'm interested in shrine and temple-themed games, and in games built on traditional music or rhythm systems such as gamelan timing.
I'm trying to find a reliable way to tell whether a game's mechanics are specific to a place or whether only its setting is.
I'm slower to reply than usual for the next few weeks because my time and energy are stretched.
I'm training for a sprint triathlon in about eight weeks and my swim training is behind. A swim buddy or a bit of coaching would help.
I still haven't booked a hotel for Shanghai and would welcome a recommendation near the festival.
I know studios that are looking for an experienced lead programmer, and I'd like to know who is available.
I like collecting old Game Boy cartridges and would happily swap or talk about them.

offers.text: Eight years of game production experience across Unity, Unreal and Godot pipelines. I can give a candid read on whether a vertical slice is realistic.
A tracker of about 900 demos tagged by region, genre and team size. I can say where a game sits among comparable titles and which niches are crowded.
Relationships with festival organisers in Tokyo, Seoul, Jakarta and Shanghai, and I can introduce teams to them.
I can recommend teams to the fund's investment committee. I can't promise anything before approval.
Concrete, honest feedback on a demo: why it passed or failed our filter. Developers have told me this is rarely given.
I can introduce solo developers, artists and composers to each other when I see complementary strengths in the submissions.
I can explain this year's signing criteria in detail so applicants don't waste an application.
A collection of old Game Boy cartridges and a lot of stories about them.

catchers.hypo: I'm an illustrator with a strong, culturally rooted art style, such as heritage tile or textile motifs. I want to make a game around it but I can't code. Where do I start?
catchers.can: I can't fund art-only pitches, but I can suggest how to find a programmer and a designer, and introduce them to teams in my network who are looking for a distinctive visual identity.
catchers.confirm: Is the artist willing to join a team of at least three rather than keep sole creative control?

catchers.hypo: I'm a composer or sound designer with traditional instruments in my background. I'd like to work on a game but have no contacts in the industry.
catchers.can: I can introduce them to teams in my pipeline that have a strong slice but no original audio, and to a freelance composer friend who campaigns for musicians' access to game teams.
catchers.confirm: Does the composer have finished samples they can share, and are they open to working on a small indie budget?

catchers.hypo: We're two people, a programmer and an artist, with a playable slice that's rooted in our own city. We don't have audio or a third member. Is there any way forward?
catchers.can: I can't get them past this year's filter as a two-person team, but I can introduce them to a composer or designer so they can reach three, and tell them what the fund would need to see.
catchers.confirm: Does the slice already run end to end, and can they bring in a third member before the 2 November window closes?

catchers.hypo: I run a small games festival or showcase in Southeast or East Asia. Can you recommend teams or take part?
catchers.can: I can compare notes with the organisers I already know and suggest teams from my shortlist. I can also visit if the dates fit my travel.
catchers.confirm: Does the festival feature original, in-development games rather than only finished commercial titles?

catchers.hypo: I'm a solo developer with a strange, regionally specific game idea. Is it worth applying to your fund?
catchers.can: I can say honestly whether it would pass the first filter, and if not, help work out which roles to add, using the contacts I know.
catchers.confirm: Is there a playable vertical slice, not just a concept or pitch deck?

catchers.hypo: I organise a group of developers building shrine, temple or folk-festival themed games. Would you look at them?
catchers.can: I can look at teams with at least three members, original art and audio, and a playable slice. I can also compare them with teams recommended by a Tokyo festival organiser.
catchers.confirm: Do the teams have at least three members with original art and audio, and not just a shared theme?

catchers.hypo: I teach or mentor a games programme. My students have made good small projects, and I want to know what a publisher looks for before they apply.
catchers.can: I can walk through what separates a slice that passes the first filter from one that doesn't, and what a publisher's feedback email usually covers.
catchers.confirm: Are the students building original games in teams, not just course exercises?

catchers.hypo: I make narrative games and I'm worried nobody will pay for localisation. Does a fund like yours care?
catchers.can: I can explain how the fund treats localisation as part of the project and what small cheques usually cover.
catchers.confirm: Is the game narrative-led, with localisation planned rather than an afterthought?

forbids.text: I can't promise funding or any outcome before the investment committee has approved it.
This cycle the fund doesn't sign solo developers, art-only pitches or music-only pitches.
The fund requires teams of at least three people, a playable vertical slice, and original art and audio.
I don't work outside the fund's cheque range of USD 80k to 250k.
I don't share internal committee discussions or minutes.
I'm travelling for the Shanghai festival from 16 October and may be hard to reach then.

projects.name: Autumn scouting cycle
projects.text: Reviewing open-call submissions and attending two festivals this autumn, looking for a few places-specific games from teams with a slice, original art and original audio.
roles_needed: indie game teams of three or more

projects.name: Matching strong solo and partial teams
projects.text: An informal attempt to pair solo developers, artists and musicians from the shortlist with complementary collaborators so they can qualify as full teams.

policy.t1: When there's a real chance of fit, I'll give this year's signing criteria in detail (team size, vertical slice, original assets, what is auto-declined), the cheque range, and introductions to collaborators and festival contacts.
policy.t2: Once there's trust and I know who you are, I'll share honest opinions about how the filter works in practice and where I think it falls short, plus studios that need people.
policy.never: Cheque sizes beyond the stated range, committee minutes and internal discussions, and any family details.
